page: Microsoft Azure D4nlds_v6 is a network-optimized, low-memory virtual machine belonging to the Dnldv6 family. Built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture, the instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance does not include graphical accelerators, allocating all system resources toward direct host execution.

A key hardware element is the inclusion of a 236 GB local NVMe SSD, providing low-latency ephemeral scratch space alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. Networking features are optimized for throughput-intensive requirements, though the configuration omits complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring auxiliary networking services when external ingress is necessary.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory configuration delivers qualitative cost efficiency for processing scenarios that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. Compared to standard 1:4 general-purpose instances, this setup avoids allocating underutilized memory, lowering expenditure per compute unit. The primary operational tradeoff is the tight 8.0 GB memory ceiling, which limits usage for large in-memory caching or deep virtualization layers.

Workloads well aligned with the D4nlds_v6 include network appliances, dedicated web serving nodes, distributed compute worker nodes, continuous integration pipelines, and stateless microservices requiring fast local disk caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D4nlds_v6 is an x86_64 Intel-based virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of memory, yielding a compute-dense 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. Part of the network-optimized Dnldv6 series, it integrates 236 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage, with no bundled GPUs. Virtualized through Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is engineered to reduce infrastructure costs for workloads that demand dedicated compute and network throughput without the overhead of surplus memory. The lean 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides strong cost efficiency for CPU-centric tasks, while the constrained memory capacity represents a tradeoff against memory-heavy applications. The D4nlds_v6 is well suited for network appliances, containerized application nodes, build runners, and stateless processing jobs relying on fast ephemeral disk access.
